newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angolan diamond mine to begin production in August.
newsitem.headline: Angolan diamond mine to begin production in August.

text.p: The Catoca diamond mine in Angola will begin production in August, a company official said on Wednesday.
"We will begin production very soon," Marcelo Gomes, the chief administrative officer for Sociedade Mineira de Catoca (SMC), told Reuters.
"In as little as two weeks we should be under way."
The four companies making up SMC include the Angolan state- owned diamond company, Endiama, and the Russian state company, Almazy Rossii-Sakha, each having a 32.8 percent share in the project.

The Brazilian company Odebrecht Mining Services Inc. has a 16.4 percent share and Israel-based Dalmonty diamond cutting and polishing company was approved as a new partner in July and now has an 18 percent share, Gomes said.
"We just brought in Dalmonty," said Gomes. "We needed the money. They provide us with $25 million to keep the project going."
Gomes said project costs had been running at around $3.2 million a month, an average $700,000 monthly cost overrun, mostly due to higher transport costs.
The former rebel movement UNITA, which still controls vast stretches of the countryside including most of the area around Catoca, has not allowed the company's convoys to pass.

The company has had to fly almost everything into the remote part of Angola's Lunda Sul Province since it began readying the project in 1995. In August the company will begin making 40 flights a month just for fuel to run its generators.
But Gomes argues that the mine's profit potential is enormous and worth the $98 million investment made so far.
In the first 10 years the 66-hectare (163-acre) mine is expected to produce some 6.2 million carats worth over $472 million.
In 1997 the company expects production of $6.6 million in diamonds and in 1998 some $40 million, say company records.

Some company officials say they are worried about the most recent military clashes that have occurred between UNITA and the government less than 200 km (125 miles) to the north east in neighbouring diamond-rich Lunda Norte Province.
